quote: After standardizing all time elements to a meridian-based time according to the geographic coordinates of the study site, we showed unequivocally that the monkeys, though predominantly diurnal, exhibited activity beyond daylight hours throughout the study.
note: Licence: the PDF prints the Creative Commons Attribution License sentence ('This article is distributed under the terms of the Creative Commons Attribution License …'); the Springer page gives CC BY 2.0. Printed year 2013 (online 2012); issue 54(1) as PMC prints it. Mammal Diversity Database page opened (living). n = 24 independent events, 6 (25%) nocturnal, 18 (75%) diurnal (Results). Diurnal events were concentrated from the start of morning civil twilight to about 30 min after sunrise and from about 30 min before sunset to the end of evening civil twilight; all but one nocturnal event extended activity beyond civil twilight; post-sunset and pre-sunrise events did not consistently correspond to the illuminated moon fraction; the authors infer the site was likely a nighttime sleeping site. Two cameras at one spot only; descriptive counts, no test. Free-ranging, unhabituated, no bait or provisioning reported. Contrary to the usual strictly diurnal expectation for anthropoids.
